title: Air India Express Adds Direct Riyadh, Bahrain Flights From Thiruvananthapuram
excerpt: Air India Express will launch thrice-weekly Thiruvananthapuram–Riyadh and twice-weekly Thiruvananthapuram–Bahrain services on October 27, 2026, with bookings already open.
body:
• New direct routes: Air India Express will fly Thiruvananthapuram–Riyadh three times a week and Thiruvananthapuram–Bahrain twice a week, starting October 27, 2026.
  • Days of operation: Riyadh services run on Tuesdays, Thursdays and Saturdays; Bahrain on Thursdays and Saturdays. Bookings are already open on the airline's website.
  • Why it matters: The Riyadh link fills a long-standing gap for direct access to the Saudi capital from Kerala's capital, sitting alongside the airline's existing daily Thiruvananthapuram–Dammam service.
  • Competition on Bahrain: The airline joins Gulf Air, which already flies the route daily, giving passengers a second carrier to compare on schedules and fares.

Air India Express will begin direct services from Thiruvananthapuram to Riyadh and Bahrain on October 27, 2026, expanding the low-cost carrier's Gulf network from Kerala's capital. Thiruvananthapuram International Airport announced the rollout on October 3, confirming that bookings for both routes are open.

The Riyadh service will operate three times a week — on Tuesdays, Thursdays and Saturdays — while the Bahrain flights will run twice weekly, on Thursdays and Saturdays. According to the airport's statement, the airline's booking page already shows the Thiruvananthapuram–Riyadh sector available for travel on the October 27 start date, with fares subject to availability.

Context and background

The Riyadh connection addresses what airport authorities described as a long-standing demand for direct access to the Saudi capital from Thiruvananthapuram. Until now, passengers relied on connecting itineraries to reach Riyadh, while Air India Express's existing daily service to Dammam served eastern Saudi Arabia. The new route widens the carrier's footprint in the kingdom, where it also flies to Jeddah from other Indian cities.

"Diaspora angle Millions of Keralites live and work in the Gulf, and air connectivity is the practical backbone of that relationship — the route home for annual leave, family emergencies and festivals."

On the Bahrain route, Air India Express will compete with Gulf Air, which already operates daily flights from Thiruvananthapuram. The additional departures give passengers a second carrier to consider when comparing schedules and fares — a development that tends to sharpen pricing on Gulf corridors.

The expansion builds on a dense existing network. Thiruvananthapuram currently handles more than 250 weekly arrivals and departures to and from the Gulf, with connections to Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Doha, Muscat and Dammam — a network the airport described as vital for the city. The airport is run by TRV (Kerala) International Airport Limited under Adani Airport Holdings.

Air India Express, a Tata Group enterprise, operates more than 500 daily flights across 45 domestic and 17 international destinations with a fleet of over 100 Boeing 737 and Airbus A320 aircraft. The Gulf is its strongest international region, and the carrier has been steadily restoring and adding frequencies there through 2026.

Impact and analysis

Kerala's Gulf corridor is one of the world's busiest labor-migration routes, and non-stop frequency directly affects trip cost and convenience for workers who travel home once or twice a year. A direct Riyadh option removes a stopover from journeys that previously required a connection — saving hours of travel time and reducing the risk of missed connections, which matter disproportionately to first-time and budget travelers.

Airport authorities said the Riyadh service is expected to particularly benefit expatriates from southern Kerala and neighboring Tamil Nadu who live and work in Saudi Arabia. On Bahrain, the entry of a second carrier introduces price competition on a route where Gulf Air has had the only daily direct option from Thiruvananthapuram.

Diaspora angle

Millions of Keralites live and work in the Gulf, and air connectivity is the practical backbone of that relationship — the route home for annual leave, family emergencies and festivals. Each additional direct frequency from Thiruvananthapuram chips away at the transfer burden these travelers carry, and Riyadh and Bahrain rank among the largest Gulf employment destinations for Kerala's diaspora.

What's next

With services starting October 27, the immediate test will be load factors through the winter travel season, when Gulf–Kerala traffic peaks. If the routes perform, the pattern on this corridor suggests further frequency additions could follow. Travelers should book early: introductory fares on new Gulf routes from Kerala have historically been snapped up quickly, and prices are explicitly subject to availability.
